newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DELY VALDES KEEPS PSG UNBEATEN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DELY VALDES KEEPS PSG UNBEATEN.

text.p: Panama striker Julio Cesar Dely Valdes saved Paris St Germain's unbeaten record with a 67th-minute equaliser in the French first division leaders' 1-1 draw at Lyon on Wednesday.

PSG, who had fallen behind 10 minutes earlier to a goal from a free-kick by Franck Gava, lead the standings with 22 points, three points ahead of second-placed Bastia who were held 0-0 at home by Nantes.

Former PSG defender Franck Colleter was sent off in a controversial ending to his new club Bordeaux's shock 2-1 defeat at home by lowly Strasbourg for protesting against a penalty awarded to the visitors five minutes into injury time.
Striker Gerald Baticle scored Strasbourg's winner from the spot after Czech defender Jan Suchoparek had headed an 86th-minute equaliser.
Previously unbeaten Bordeaux, who -- like Lyon, champions Auxerre and Metz -- have 17 points, went in front in the 68th minute through Kaba Diawara.
Auxerre beat Monaco 2-0 at home with a 47th-minute strike by Bernard Diomede and an own goal by defender Emmanuel Petit 18 minutes later.
Late in the game Monaco midfielder Lilian Martin was sent off for a second bookable offence.
Marseille's Italian central defender Ivan Franceschini was also given his marching orders, ordered off in the 45th minute of his side's 2-1 home win over Guingamp.
